item.title: Managing Under Political Turbulence
item.content:encoded:
Jonathan Doh, Villanova University

Srividya Jandhyala, ESSEC Business School

Yadong Luo, University of Miami

Grazia D. Santangelo, Copenhagen Business School

Rising political turbulence globally—including violent conflicts, regime changes, geopolitical tensions, and trade wars—increasingly affects organizations across sectors. This special issue seeks evidence-based insights to help managers and organizations navigate these challenges, filling the gap between academic theory and practical managerial guidance on operating effectively under political turbulence.

The special issue welcomes rigorous submissions addressing how organizations and managers can understand, influence, and adapt to political risks and disruptions. Papers should provide actionable insights grounded in robust empirical evidence or conceptual frameworks, directly addressing real-world managerial and policy issues. The journal prioritizes practitioner-accessible work that guides organizational behavior and policy decisions rather than theory-driven research.

Appel publié par Academy of Management Perspectives. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Understanding different types and forms of political turbulence and their classification
  • Rethinking corporate political strategies and integration of political activities
  • Reorganizing and realigning geographically diversified operations in response to political change
  • Managing stakeholder nationalism and organizational political positioning
  • The role of new technologies (AI, blockchain, digital intelligence) in political risk management
  • Managing corporate innovation while navigating national security and political constraints
  • Navigating talent management and migration under anti-immigration political turbulence

Timeline

  • September 1, 2026: Submission window opens
  • September 30, 2026: Final submission deadline at 23:59 ET (DST+1, UTC-4)

Associate editors

  • Tazeeb Rajwani, University of Surrey

item.title: Turning Implications Into Evidence: Actionable Solutions to Real-World Problems of Practice and Policy Based on Prior Academy of Management Publications
item.content:encoded:
Julian Birkinshaw, Western University

Thomas P. Lyon, University of Michigan

Denise M. Rousseau, Carnegie Mellon University

Majken Schultz, Copenhagen Business School

Mo Wang, University of Florida

This special issue seeks original research that transforms previously published managerial implications from Academy of Management journals into validated, actionable solutions. Rather than leaving implications as speculative statements, the issue invites scholars to conduct rigorous empirical or conceptual research that develops evidence-based guidance for practitioners and policy makers on real-world problems of practice and policy.

The special issue reflects the Academy of Management's commitment to producing not just valid knowledge but also knowledge that is usable outside academia. Papers should build on theory from AOM journals while enhancing these theories by revealing their practical boundaries and nuances, ultimately strengthening the relevance and value of management scholarship.

Appel publié par Academy of Management Perspectives. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Developing actionable solutions from managerial implications published in Academy of Management journals
  • Conducting novel empirical or conceptual analysis on practice and policy problems identified in prior AOM publications
  • Creating robust evidence and guidance for practitioners and policy makers based on underdeveloped or dormant implications
  • Analyzing practice and policy implications from Academy of Management Annals, Collections, Discoveries, Journal, Learning & Education, Review, or Perspectives

Timeline

  • January 1, 2027: Submission window opens
  • February 1, 2027: Submission deadline

Associate editors

  • Michael L. Barnett, Rutgers University

item.title: Open Call for Papers
item.content:encoded:
Academy of Management Perspectives seeks manuscripts that prioritize relevance to managerial practice and policy. The journal explicitly rejects papers that are primarily theory-driven or that repurpose work rejected by other journals by adding managerial implications as an afterthought. Papers must be managerially motivated from inception, addressing specific issues that inform how organizations are managed.

Beyond relevance, AMP demands rigorous original analysis using evidence-based findings rather than opinions or philosophical arguments. This rigor may emerge from empirical research or robust conceptual frameworks, comparable to standards at elite journals.

AMP papers must be relevant, rigorous, and readable. They simultaneously address important managerial issues, employ original scholarly analysis, and communicate findings accessibly to practitioners through plain language and concise presentation.

Appel publié par Academy of Management Perspectives. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Papers that inform managerial practice and policy
  • Studies addressing issues of importance to managers and policy makers
  • Work demonstrating how organizations can be better managed and governed
  • Research providing evidence to drive reconsideration of managerial practices
  • Papers bridging scholarly analysis with practitioner insights
  • Studies avoiding theory-driven approaches disconnected from practice
  • Conceptual or empirical analysis grounded in real-world managerial challenges

Timeline

  • January 31, 2027: Submission Deadline
